newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper opens "highway through hell".
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper opens "highway through hell".

text.p: President Ernesto Samper on Wednesday inaugurated a $276 million highway project that cuts through the heart of Colombia's badlands -- a stronghold of right-wing paramilitary groups.

The 186 mile (300 km) stretch through the Magdalena Medio area in the centre of the country is one of the final pieces of the jigsaw in the effort to link Colombia's Caribbean coast to its southern border with Ecuador.
The trans-Colombia highway is scheduled for completion by early 1997 and will be about 950 miles (1,500 km) long -- the longest in the country -- the National Roads Institute says.

Construction has taken more than 15 years because of delays caused by simmering guerrilla war, planning problems and financial shortfalls, a spokeswoman at the Institute said. Estimates of the overall cost are not available.

The Magdalena Medio has been a focus for paramilitary activity for more than a decade. In the mid-1980s, landowners and cattle ranchers in league with drug barons and allegedly with members of the armed forces unleashed a fight to the death to clear the region of leftist guerrillas, a task which they seem to have largely achieved.
